In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of vegetation on nesting success of greater sage-grouse.
the relationship between vegetation structure surrounding the nest and nest success in greater sage-grouse (Centorcercus urophasionus).
the relationship between grass cover and nest success for a species that is declining throughout much of its range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of grass height around sage‐grouses’ nests is unknown, but it is unlikely that it is as large as previously thought, especially in areas where the sage‐grouseeither has not been present or where it is not currently present.
the evidence is equivocal for a biological effect of grasses surrounding nests on nest success in sage‐grouses.
the relationship between grass heights and nest survival in sage‐grouses is not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of grass height is not ubiquitous across time or space.
the relationship between grass cover and greater sage‐grous nest success is likely to be confounded by phenology and that management recommendations for grass height should be reconsidered.
the effect of grass height surrounding sage‐grouses' nests on their nest success is not well understood, and that further research is needed to determine if and how grass height affects nest success.
The main takeaway from our work is that

managers should be cautious when using grass height as a surrogate for concealment, as there are many factors that influence concealment, and grass height is not the only factor that should be considered when managing for greater sage‐gouge nest success.

managers should not rely on grass height alone to inform habitat management to promote sage‐grouses and should consider other factors that may be more influential on nest concealment and nest survival.
managers should be cautious when interpreting grass height as an important predictor of sage‐grouss nest success, and should consider alternative predictors that may be more robust to temporal bias.
